summary: Exact census (C sieve-factorisation of N_C=4Cp+1, scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z3072_omega.c, validated against sympy): 300 primes p≡1 (4) just above 10⁹ and 150 Mordell-hard (square classes mod 840) primes, all C ≤ 10⁵ (4.5·10⁷ pairs), plus full C-ranges for 3642 primes in [10⁶,1.1·10⁶] and 282 near 10⁷. Premise verified: P(certificate | Ω=1) = 0 exactly (PROVED, divisors of a prime N are 1, N ≡ 1 mod 4C; 1.84·10⁶ cases at 10⁹). Within each C-decade P rises smoothly with k (e.g. C∈[10,100): k=2..7 → 0.0098, 0.031, 0.068, 0.135, 0.222, 0.297; C∈[1,10): 0.16, 0.35, 0.56, 0.77), tracking the shape of the uniform-class model 1−(1−1/φ(4C))^{2^{k−1}−1} at 0.5–0.6× its value (EVIDENCE); no even/odd alternation, hard classes mod 840 match the rest within noise. Unconditioned on C the marginal P(cert|k) is dominated by the C-mix (0.0001 at k=3 to 0.003 at k=11, data/z52b/pass2/ZF1/Z3072/summary.txt).
not_done: No primes beyond 1.0001·10⁹ (300+150 primes only); no k-table for C > 10⁵ at 10⁹; the uniform-class model is a crude squarefree approximation (not fitted).
next: Use the per-(k,C) table as the baseline for any sieve-weight lower bound on Σ_C 1[r_C>0].

summary: Did the parity test at fixed sieve data (same programs as Z3072): write N_C = s·r with s the N^{1/3}-smooth part, r the rough part (Ω(r) ≤ 2). PROVED (elementary): N ≡ 1 (mod 4C) forces r ≡ s⁻¹, so when Ω(r) ≤ 1 success at C is a function of (s, C) alone; the only sieve-invisible information is the split r = r₁r₂ (Ω(r)=2) — exactly Selberg's parity datum. EVIDENCE: at the same τ(s)- and C-stratum, Ω(r)=2 raises success 1.8–6× over Ω(r)=1 (e.g. τ(s)=2, C∈[10,100): 0.0058 vs 0.036), the Liouville marginal is blind (P = 0.00022 vs 0.00022 at 10⁹), and 82–86 % of certificates are decided by s (10⁶ full ranges: 80.7 %, 10⁷: 82.1 %); but p = 1044877 (≡ 757 mod 840) has R(p) > 0 with all 5 certificate levels (C = 1, 3, 68, 3958, 130610) parity-invisible, 1 of 3642 primes in [10⁶,1.1·10⁶] (0 of 282 near 10⁷, min 4 visible levels). So a sieve/parity-blind argument at level N^{1/3} cannot certify every prime, although parity affects only ≈ 1/5 of certificates on average (Assessment); the odd-square (T1) obstruction is not of parity type (it has identical 1-dimensional sieve densities over C, ρ(ℓ)=1 for ℓ ∤ 2m, and kills all Ω).
not_done: 'Visible' is defined only for the cut z = N^{1/3} (no scan over z); no literature theorem (Friedlander–Iwaniec Opera de Cribro ch. 16 parity) was read beyond the standard statement; frequency of zero-visible primes above 10⁶ not estimated (only 282 primes at 10⁷).
next: Scan the cut z = N^θ and count zero-visible primes in [10⁶,10⁷] to see whether parity-invisible primes thin out.

summary: Implemented R_w(p) = Σ w over (★) triples for 8 weights on the log-simplex (x,y,z) = (ln u, ln B, ln C)/ln(p/4) (sharp; Gaussians σ = .15/.25/.40 at the barycentre; smoothstep edge ramps η = .1/.2, with zero or half weight at the boundary; 27xyz) and main terms M_w = Σ w/φ(4uB) over the pair form, for all primes p ≡ 1 (4) in [10⁷, 1.1·10⁷] (30 899) and [10⁸, 1.01·10⁸] (27 101), scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z2902_rw.c (R checked against sympy). Smoothing barely moves the left tail: the 0.1 % quantile of R_w/M_w is 0.255 → 0.282 (best: half-weight edge ramp) at 10⁷ and 0.314 → 0.343 at 10⁸, and (mean − q.001)/sd stays 2.2–2.7 for every weight; R_w > 0 at all primes for all weights. What smoothing does change is the variance structure: Var/Poisson falls from 5.0–5.9 (sharp) to 1.9–2.4 for boundary-vanishing weights and the Mordell-hard-class deficit (mean ratio 0.74–0.78 for sharp) becomes 0.91–0.99 — the over-dispersion and the hard-class effect live on the simplex boundary (exact source identified under Z2080: the u = 1 / B = 1 lines are divisors of p + 1).
not_done: No true Beurling–Selberg majorant/minorant (only smooth bumps/ramps); weights depend on log-coordinates only; no optimisation over a weight family; main term uses the p-independent density 1/φ(4uB) (no BM χ-correction), so part of the sharp-weight variance is the BM term.
next: If a weighted R_w is used analytically, take the half-weight edge ramp (or treat the p+1 edge lines exactly) — the left tail does not improve beyond ≈ 10 %.

summary: Read Friedlander–Iwaniec arXiv:1807.06648 (Bredihin/Linnik): the dispersion step is now divisor switching (their (2.4), moduli ≤ 2√X) + the BFI bound (3.1) Σ_{q≤√x(log x)^A}|π(x;q,a) − π(x)/φ(q)| ≪ x(log log x/log x)² for a FIXED residue a; in ES (trial form p ≡ −u mod 4uC−1) there is no long prime variable at fixed p, the residue is tied to the modulus, and moduli reach ≈ p^{2/3} after switching, so only almost-all statements could follow (Assessment). Second moment of S = R/2 by level C over all primes p ≡ 1 (4) in [10⁷,1.1·10⁷] and [10⁸,1.01·10⁸]: Var/Mean = 2.28 / 2.70 (1.67 / 2.08 after mod-840 class means); levels C ≥ 32 are individually Poisson (Var/Mean 0.96–1.09), C = 1, 2 are 3.8, 2.6; cross-level covariance carries 33–38 % of Var S. The over-dispersion has an exact source: the edge lines u = 1 or B = 1 are E(p) = #{d | p+1 : d ≡ 3 (mod 4)} (PROVED, B(4C−1) = p+1), with Var/Mean 5.5 / 7.3, explaining 44 % of Var S; the interior S − E is near-Poisson (index 1.69 / 1.94; 1.39 / 1.65 after mod 840), corr(E, S−E) = −0.13 (EVIDENCE).
not_done: Linnik's original dispersion inequality (book ch. 7) not read — only the FI modern replacement; no BV-type discrepancy sum over the tied progressions computed; edge share not computed beyond 10⁸.
next: Model R = E(p+1-divisors) + near-Poisson interior and test the (★) census zeros against it.

summary: Wrote scripts/es_forms.py: exact converters solution ↔ ET Type I (a,b,c,d,t) ↔ Type I divisor form (f g = n² + 4c²d, f ≡ g ≡ −n mod 4cd) ↔ Type I e-slice, solution ↔ ET Type II (a,b,c,d,e) ↔ Type II divisor form (f g = 4c²dn + 1, f ≡ g ≡ −1 mod 4cd) ↔ Type II e-slice, and ET-II(c=1) ↔ (★) (u,B,C) ↔ C-form (C, a) ↔ SL₂ matrix ↔ level-4C word; canonical inverses via d = gcd of reduced denominators. Round-trip test: all 159 617 solutions of all odd n ≤ 1201 (14 929 Type I, 5 823 Type II, 138 865 neither — composites), every C-form at 41 primes near 10⁵ (469), T1 (no Type I/II at odd squares) and 'every prime solution is I or II' asserted; ordered f_II matches the independent scripts/bs_adv_count.c at p = 409, 1009, 2521 (12, 16, 6). Only noteworthy item: 287 (★) solutions at composite n ≤ 1201 are not ET Type II in the coprime sense (e.g. n = 21: (6, 63, 126)) — the known R290 nuance, not a new fact.
not_done: No continued-fraction/ES₅, lattice, quaternion or theta-quotient forms (no element-level dictionary exists in the repo); no wiki page written.
next: Add the ES₅ five-slice and theta-coefficient views once an element-level map is fixed.

summary: Exponent-covering search for I3 (n = tuv−u−v, t,u,v ≥ 3) with all two-fixed-coordinate words (E: uv | n+u+v; L: (tu−1) | n+u), moduli ≤ 3000–12000 incl. those sharing primes with the base (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z2776_i3cover.py; positive controls 2^k±1, 3·2^k+1 reproduce I3_DEEP_FABLE Thm 5.5). PROVED (computer-assisted): I3(3^k+2) ≥ 1 for all k ≥ 3, k ≠ 4, by three L-words of period 12 [(3,3), (4,4), (13,7)]; also 5·3^k−1 and 2·3^k+1 close (L = 12). 3^k−2 is covered except k ≡ 1 (mod 240), 5·3^k+1 except k ≡ 1, 2 (mod 48), 3^k−1 except k ≡ 1 (mod 48); the residual limit points equal tiny I3 zeros (1, 16, 46, 2, …) away from 3 and lie in no word class of modulus ≤ 3·10⁶, and for 3^k−2 I PROVED (root-splitting mod prime powers) that the point (1 at p≠3, −2 at 3) lies in no E- or L-class at all, so no fixed-word exponent covering of 3^k−2 exists (md_S6.md §Z2776).
not_done: No moving-word (window) search for the residual classes; sterility proofs for the points of 3^k−1, 5·3^k+1, 3^k+1 not written (EVIDENCE only); 5^k±1 only at B = 3000; the 3^k+2 proof is not formalised in Lean and has no independent second checker beyond direct division for k ≤ 400.
next: Search moving words for n = 3X²−2, X = 3^j (the I3 analogue of the Sophie-Germain window) on the residual class k ≡ 1.
